title: Shard size mismatch — ad-hoc debug diary
content:
Goal: get reproducible, minimal repro and a reliable repair path for a model load failure that appears only on some hosts.

Summary: intermittent model load failures when streaming checkpoint shards from GCS. Error seen in runtime: "RuntimeError: expected shard size 524288000 but got 524288320" (sizes vary). Only repros on a subset of machines (we think different Linux kernels + gcsfuse versions). Hypothesis: one of the shards has extra bytes (alignment/padding/gzip header) introduced during upload or during a recompose operation.

What I saw (notes from repro run on host-a around 2024-11-11 09:12):
- Model: llama-13b-v2-like (open format) packaged as tar+manifest with shards: model.ckpt.tar.zst.part-0000..part-0011.
- Manifest declares shard byte sizes and checksums. loader verifies each shard length against manifest then streams and builds mmapped weights.
- Failure occurs during verify "read_exact" when comparing expected length to actual object size from GCS HEAD.

Example error (exact copy):
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/redwood/runtime/load.py", line 412, in load_checkpoint_streaming
    assert blob_size == expected, f"expected shard size {expected} but got {blob_size}"
AssertionError: expected shard size 524288000 but got 524288320

Immediate hypotheses:
1) Upload time padding: some uploader (gsutil -m compose or a custom compose) may have concatenated chunks with overlapping bytes or added gzip headers.
2) Client-side transfer tools (gcsfuse / curl) injecting extra bytes or metadata when doing streaming reads.
3) Manifest generation bug: manifest lists uncompressed size but object stored is compressed (or vice versa).
4) Truncation vs padding: some transfers produced slightly larger file (320 bytes extra) — could be metadata footer from zstd tool or mis-handled block alignment.

Commands I ran (repro attempts and inspection):
- List object and size via gcloud storage and gsutil:
  $ gsutil ls -l gs://redwood-checkpoints/llama-13b/run123/model.ckpt.tar.zst.part-0007
  524288320  2024-11-10T21:03:12Z  gs://redwood-checkpoints/llama-13b/run123/model.ckpt.tar.zst.part-0007

- Compare HEAD metadata returned by storage client in runtime vs gsutil:
  $ python -c "from google.cloud import storage; b=storage.Client().bucket('redwood-checkpoints').blob('llama-13b/run123/model.ckpt.tar.zst.part-0007'); b.reload(); print(b.size)"
  -> 524288320

- Download head/tail bytes to inspect footers (use dd + hexdump):
  $ gsutil cp gs://.../part-0007 /tmp/part-0007.bin
  $ tail -c 512 /tmp/part-0007.bin | hexdump -C | sed -n '1,40p'
  Observed repeating pattern: 0000... and small ascii fragment "zstd" near tail in one copy.

- Re-downloaded the object from a different region host (host-b): size reported 524288000 and checksums matched manifest. So the object on storage appears to differ depending on which path (eg staging vs compose?).

- Ran `gsutil hash -m` on the two copies (from host-a and host-b): different CRC32C and MD5 for the same object name when downloaded via different proxies. Suspicious.

- Looked into artifacts directory: found both "part-0007" and "part-0007.composed". The uploader step (pipeline/compose.sh) is using `gsutil compose` to combine temporary chunks (tmp-*). We have a known flaky compose job that retries with overlapping window; ticket CKPT-395 is relevant.

Quick experiments:
- Recompose locally: re-run `gsutil compose tmp-000[0-3] model.ckpt.tar.zst.part-0007` and check size. Recompose produced 524288000 (expected).
- Snapshot of object metadata before/after compose: previous object had generation # 17012345; after recompose new generation with expected size. But the failing hosts still saw the old size for a short window (eventual consistency?).

Things that confound:
- GCS is strongly consistent for object creation/deletion since 2020, so seeing two sizes for same object name is strange. However, `gsutil -m cp` sometimes creates temporary object names then renames; in our uploader we use `compose` and then `mv` semantics implemented by copy+delete. Race condition possible if loaders read while compose is in-progress.

Repro plan steps (minimal):
1) On staging bucket, run compose job while concurrently issuing HEAD requests from a small Python script with a tight loop to catch transient sizes.
2) Run this from multiple regions (us-central1, europe-west1) and log generation numbers returned.
3) If mismatch seen, attempt to `gcloud storage objects rewrite` to atomicize final object and verify loader behavior.

Notes on kernel/gcsfuse theory:
- Some failing hosts run gcsfuse and read via FUSE mount; others stream via cloud storage API directly. FUSE could have caching or read-size rounding that makes loader read an extra block when reading via prefetch. But the blob HEAD size query uses storage API, so mismatch shouldn't be due to FUSE reads unless the FUSE mount is a hidden intermediary used by the uploader.

Commands to collect more telemetry (ad-hoc script):
- head_probe.py (rough):
  for i in range(200):
    b = storage.Client().bucket(B).blob(PATH); b.reload(); print(i, time.time(), b.size, b.generation)
    time.sleep(0.2)
- also run `gsutil stat -r gs://bucket/path` and `curl -I "https://storage.googleapis.com/bucket/path"` to see response headers X-Goog-Generation etc.

Potential quick fixes:
- Loader: change assert -> permissive path that streams up to min(expected, actual) and then validate checksum of content rather than relying solely on size. If checksum fails, try refetch. This trades a little complexity for resilience.
- Uploader: make compose step atomic by writing to a temp object name and then `rewrite` to final name or use generation-aware checks. Add a short backoff before marking manifest as ready.

Evidence for manifest-version confusion:
- Manifest file line: `part-0007 524288000 sha256:abc123` but in one session the object had extra 320 bytes and sha256 different. That suggests object mutated after manifest generation or a different object exists with same name.

Remaining unknowns / TODOs: (priority order)
- [ ] Reproduce transient size flip reliably with small compose loop + parallel HEAD probes (priority: high).
- [ ] Capture X-Goog-Generation values at time of failure on failing hosts (add instrumentation to loader to log generation + size + crc).
- [ ] Add loader retry that on size mismatch performs b.reload() + sleep + recheck up to 3 times, logging generation changes. Quick patch in runtime to mitigate in prod.
- [ ] Audit uploader pipeline for any `-n` flags or streaming zstd wrappers that might append small footers on some runs (check CI image versions).
- [ ] Try `gcloud storage rewrite` for a known-good object and see if failing hosts still observe wrong size (to test caching/proxy issue).

Notes / random observations:
- Observed a different oddball: one object had extra 64 bytes with ASCII "PATCHED_BY_PIPELINE" near EOF. That definitely points to a buggy compose script that accidentally echoes a string into the file when combining. Need to grep pipeline logs for any stray `echo` or printf.

Meeting notes to escalate:
- Ping infra (Samir) for uploader logs.
- Add an alert that flags checkpoint load size mismatches > 0.1% frequency across hosts.

Short-term mitigation (candidate): change runtime assert to:
- if blob_size != expected:
    log.warn(..., generation=b.generation, observed=blob_size)
    for attempt in 1..3: b.reload(); if b.size == expected: continue load; sleep(0.5 * attempt)
    otherwise fetch blob and verify sha256; if sha matches: accept; else raise detailed error and queue re-download + recreate manifest.

Long-term: ensure uploader pipeline does atomic finalization, and add post-upload verification step that loads first/last 32 bytes and checksum to detect accidental footers.

Appendix — raw snippets I pasted into slack: (kept for context)
- "seeing blob size 524288320 on host-a, 524288000 on host-b for same name. gsutil shows 320 too. recompose locally to expected size. trace points to compose step that runs on uploader."
- "found \"PATCHED_BY_PIPELINE\" in one tail sample — grep the compose scripts for echo / printf."

If you pick this up: check CKPT-395 and the compose.sh in infra-artifacts pipeline. I left a copy of the sample part file in /tmp/inspect/part-0007.* on host-a (FYI).

End diary entry (for now) — Violet
